title: Morton on boogie-woogie players and on Handy and the blues
summary: Morton's remark about boogie pianists who only know one trick, and his view that blues was disreputable until Handy made money from it.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Kansas City Jazz. I don't know whether you read it or not. I wrote that first little thing I wrote for the record changer was just a little paragraph about Johnny being in New York. And he went to a nightclub where a couple of boogie woogie players were the star attraction. I guess they were the only thing there. And they were playing the boogie woogie stuff. And Johnny got persuaded to give a few examples of his stuff. You know, he played and went over all right. And he was telling Lomax about playing there, you know. And Johnny says, well, he says, did you do all right? Johnny says, yes, I did all right. He says, did you do all right? He says, do all right in comparison to those boogie players? Johnny says, sure, I did all right with those boogie players. And Lomax coming up, he says, did you? Did you do as well or do as good as those boogie woogie players? He said, why shouldn't I do as good as guys that only know one, too? It was true.
Why shouldn't he tell the term of that? He's probably talking about Ammons and Johnson.

It might have been Ammons and Johnson, or Johnson and Turner. Who was it? There's a couple of them that were playing around New York. Yeah, they were around. Anyhow, the guys that only know one, too. That's what got it with Handy, too, you know. Because Handy hadn't really done something with it. The blues made plenty of money out of it. Johnny said, blues wasn't considered music in those days, which was a fact. They'd hush you up as you started playing it down there and go on and that kind of thing. And also, I think it was Mudd Carey, they quote him as saying blues, and they said only the ignorant played blues. But when Handy showed you could make some money out of it, then everybody began to get it through. And it certainly did spread it.
